title: define-phased-acceptance-lanes-and-dependency-owners-for-prd-scope-flex
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Objective: Create a clear, phased acceptance framework for the upcoming PRD (Scope Flex) so PM/Eng/Design/Legal sign-offs are deterministic and scoped per lane. The PRD introduces a scope-flex model (basic->recommended->enterprise) where features can be trimmed or ramped based on regulatory or latency constraints. This ticket captures acceptance lanes, owner assignments for each dependency, legal checkpoints for data residency and usage terms, and explicit exit criteria for sign-off at every lane. The goal is to reduce last-minute scope churn by making acceptance contracts explicit and traceable.
acceptance_criteria: Three acceptance lanes defined with concrete criteria: Basic (MVP), Recommended (default user experience), Enterprise (compliance/SLA features)
For each lane: assigned owner (eng/design/legal), checklist of deliverables, and target test matrix (functional + perf + privacy)
Design artifacts linked and reviewed: annotated flows, accessibility notes, and error-state mocks for each lane
Engineering feasibility doc with quantified perf delta and known trade-offs for feature toggles
Legal sign-off checklist completed for data residency, contract language, and marketing claims for Enterprise lane
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with PM/ENG/DES/LEGAL. Aligned on the three-lane approach and that Basic must not require additional infra changes.
2026-02-26: Design capacity meeting — DES noted that Recommended requires an additional confirmation modal and two new microcopy strings (DES-4421).
2026-03-01: Engineering feasibility spike finished (ENG-33421) — estimated +12% token latency for Recommended when KV prefix caching disabled; enterprise will need KV isolation work.
2026-03-05: Legal sent initial redlines on data-retention language and flagged analytics export as restricted for Enterprise in EU regions (LEGAL-78).
2026-03-10: Cross-team review session. Decided to gate Enterprise rollout on completion of a short privacy attestation and a regional export blocklist. Marco to coordinate eng tasks.
2026-03-12: PRD v0.3 posted to Confluence with acceptance lanes, owners, and initial checklists. Requesting formal sign-off invites to be sent to owners by 2026-03-15.
comments: Sofia Patel (PM): 'We need deterministic signoffs — if Legal flags a term, we should be able to ship Basic and Recommended with a documented exception path.'
Evan Park (Engineering): 'Recommend a canary strategy for Recommended; we'll surface latency regressions in telemetry prior to Enterprise rollout.'
Ava Martinez (Design): 'I'll add alternate copy for the modal flows and stack the accessibility checklist; need 3 days to finalize mocks.'
Rachel Gold (Legal): 'Enterprise claims must avoid implying data residency beyond contractual terms. I'll propose contract language next week.'
decision_points: Whether Basic lane can bypass KV caching changes (ENG decided Basic must not require infra changes)
Approve the legal fallback language for Recommended marketing copy
Define rollout criteria (telemetry thresholds) that will gate Recommended -> Enterprise
risks: If Legal holds Enterprise signoff late, product may ship without enterprise features causing contract delays
Recommended lane increases tail latency in specific prompt shapes; risk of SLA regressions unless telemetry gating is enforced
Design gaps for error states could increase support tickets post-launch
